record.original_question: Extend the Euclidean theory of paracommutators from R^n to stratified groups G, such as the Heisenberg group. In particular, for kernels K that are homogeneous of degree -2Q on G x G and paracommutators T_b = T_b(K) defined from left translations and dilations, determine explicit hypotheses on K and the correct Besov-type spaces for b under which one obtains a full analogue of the Section 1 theory, including Schatten-class criteria beyond the p = 2 case and the needed minimality and maximality properties of the underlying function spaces.

evidence.quote: In this case we can no longer make use of the Fourier transform or at least it is less suitable here. However, we conjecture that most of the previous theory (see Section 1) carries over to the present situation.

To proceed further we need also the minimality of the space B^0_1 or, what is the same, the maximality of dually related spaces. It is also clear that the assumptions on K are less explicit than in the case of R^n, in which case they were formulated in terms of A (see Section 1). We therefore postpone a further treatment to a future occasion.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G be a stratified Lie group (for example, the Heisenberg group H^n) of homogeneous dimension Q, equipped with left translations τ_g (g ∈ G) and the natural family of dilations δ_t (t > 0). For a measurable kernel K : G × G → C that is jointly homogeneous of degree −2Q with respect to the dilations and suitably translation-covariant, and for a locally integrable symbol b on G, define the paracommutator T_b = T_b(K) acting on test functions f on G by

    (T_b f)(x) = ∫_{G × G} K(x,y) b(z) (something built from left translations and dilations of f and b) dμ(y) dμ(z),

modeled on the Euclidean paracommutator construction T_b(K)f = ∫∫ K(ξ,η) â(ξ,η) b̂(ξ−η) f̂(η) e^{i⟨x,ξ⟩} dξ dη but rewritten on G using convolution structure rather than Fourier transform, so that T_b is bilinear in (K, b), linear in f, and commutes with the joint G-action by left translation and the joint scaling by δ_t (with the appropriate weight).

Problem. Identify:

(a) explicit, checkable hypotheses on the kernel K (analogues, on G × G, of the Euclidean conditions on the symbol A which control non-degeneracy, smoothness off the diagonal, and homogeneity), and

(b) a scale of homogeneous Besov-type function spaces B^{s}_{p,q}(G) on the stratified group G,

such that the following analogues of the Euclidean paracommutator theory hold:

  (i) Boundedness: T_b is bounded on L^2(G) if and only if b lies in the appropriate B^{0}_{∞,∞}-type space on G;
  (ii) Schatten class membership: for all 0 < p < ∞ (in particular for p ≠ 2), T_b belongs to the Schatten ideal S_p(L^2(G)) if and only if b lies in a homogeneous Besov space B^{Q/p}_{p,p}(G) (or its correct analogue);
  (iii) Minimality/maximality: the Besov space B^{0}_{1} appearing as the symbol class in (ii) for the endpoint is minimal among translation- and dilation-invariant symbol spaces giving trace-class T_b, and its dual is correspondingly maximal;
  (iv) Cut-off/decomposition tools replacing Fourier analysis (e.g. Littlewood–Paley theory on G, sub-Laplacian heat-kernel decompositions) suffice to obtain these characterizations without recourse to the Euclidean Fourier transform.

Determine the precise hypotheses on K and the precise Besov spaces on G for which (i)–(iv) hold in full generality on every stratified Lie group G.
artifact.status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made for specific paracommutator-type operators on stratified groups: Schatten-class characterizations for commutators of Riesz transforms on the Heisenberg group (Fan–Lacey–Li–Wick, 2021/2023) and more general Calderón–Zygmund commutators on stratified Lie groups (2024) are now available, with symbols characterized via Besov-type norms and methods (Schrödinger representations, double operator integrals, Alpert/NWO bases) that bypass Fourier analysis. However, a complete general theory for arbitrary paracommutators T_b(K) with arbitrary admissible homogeneous kernels K on a general stratified group, including the minimality/maximality of the endpoint Besov space and the full range p ≠ 2, does not appear to be settled in the literature; the existing results cover important special cases rather than the full conjectured analogue.

status_evidence.title: Schatten classes and commutators of Riesz transform on Heisenberg group and applications
status_evidence.snippet: Schatten norm of commutators with Riesz transforms on the Heisenberg group is characterized in terms of Besov norms of the symbol, generalizing Peller and Janson–Wolff type results without Fourier analysis.
status_evidence.claim: Schatten/Besov characterization of certain paracommutator-type operators is established on the Heisenberg group, covering a key case of the problem.

status_evidence.title: Schatten properties of Calderón–Zygmund singular integral commutator on stratified Lie groups
status_evidence.snippet: Schatten estimates of Calderón–Zygmund singular integral commutators are obtained on general stratified Lie groups using Alpert bases and NWO sequences.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work extends Schatten-class results for commutators to general stratified Lie groups, addressing parts (i)–(ii) for a class of kernels.

status_evidence.title: Paracommutators and Minimal Spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of paracommutators and minimality of the symbol space B^0_1 in the Euclidean setting, with the stratified-group case left open.
status_evidence.claim: The minimality/maximality aspect of the paracommutator theory on stratified groups is identified as not fully resolved.
